SCRIPE Authorization, Entitlements & Multi-Role RBAC Remediation

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE enforces fail-closed authorization across 490 permissions, 190 features, 16 internal roles, and 10 UserGroups. Every boundary preserves dotted FLS keys, non-destructive feature toggles, and post-commit cache invalidation.

  1. Core.Application catalog reconciliation leaves 0 broken RequiredFeature links and classifies 56 literal-unreferenced permissions with 0 exceptions.
  2. scripe-internal activates 389 tenant-safe permissions while quarantining 69 PlatformOnly permissions and disabling Marketplace (18) and Plugins (14).
  3. TenantContextMiddleware runs pre-authorization with cold-cache warming and fail-closed HttpFeatureChecker live feature verification.
  4. AdminSecurityService orders roles by ascending Priority (0 = highest), intersects read FLS masks across roles, and unions additive UserGroup caps without truncating dotted resource keys.

Applies toSCRIPE monorepo490 perms16 roles10 groups

Request ingress, catalog metadata, live Entitlements checks, multi-role FLS merges, and post-commit cache eviction run across explicit module boundaries without violating Clean Architecture.

  1. Next.js 16 MVVM Portal ↗

    Enforces tenant SuperAdmin separation and fail-closed PAGE_PERMISSIONS, paired with the dedicated frontend-rbac-superadmin-fls-mvvm board.

  2. Tenant Context & MFA Gate ↗

    Skips anonymous routes, cold-warms AdminPermissionCache, and validates bidirectional MembershipMode before UseAuthorization.

  3. Permission Authz Handler ↗

    Evaluates RequiredAnyFeatures, IsGloballyAvailable, and fail-closed IFeatureChecker plus pat_scope intersection.

  4. FLS Merge Engine ↗

    Unions masks within each role, intersects across read-capable roles by ascending Priority, and keeps dotted keys like crm.opportunities.

  5. Effective Feature Builder ↗

    Commits overrides and edition updates in EntitlementsDbContext before emitting post-commit SubscriptionChanged events.

How do cross-tenant requests and cache invalidation execute in order?

Diagram structure
  • Next.js 16 Client spa
  • TenantContext MW ctx_mw
  • Authz Handler authz
  • FLS & Export Guard fls
  • Entitlements ent
  • Cache & DB cache
  • spa → ctx_mw · GET /crm/opportunities + X-Tenant-Context
  • ctx_mw → cache · Warm AdminPermissionCache + Load Membership
  • cache → ctx_mw · Target EffectivePermissions + FLS
  • ctx_mw → authz · RequireMfa -> UseAuthorization
  • authz → ent · IFeatureChecker.IsEnabledAsync(TargetTenant, CRM.Enabled)
  • authz → fls · Resolve [Resource] -> crm.opportunities
  • fls → cache · Read-Preferred Intersect + Group Union
  • fls → spa · 200 JSON (masked FLS) or CSV Neutralized
  • spa → ent · SetFeatureOverride(CRM.Enabled = false)
  • ent → cache · SaveChangesAsync -> Invalidate FeatureCache
  • ent → cache · SubscriptionChanged -> Sync Pool (Keep RolePerms)
  • cache → spa · Evict AdminCache + admin:principal:* Stamp
  • spa → authz · Stale JWT Re-Test -> 403 Forbidden

Middleware establishes authoritative context first, live feature gates reject disabled modules immediately, and override mutations commit to the database before clearing caches and version stamps.

  1. Inbound Switch Request ↗

    Next.js attaches X-Tenant-Context on GET /crm/opportunities.

  2. Cold-Cache Context Warm ↗

    TenantContextMiddleware warms AdminPermissionCache before verifying target membership so cache eviction never triggers false 403 responses.

  3. Live Entitlements Check ↗

    PermissionAuthorizationHandler verifies IFeatureChecker.IsEnabledAsync(TargetTenant, CRM.Enabled) instead of trusting JWT claims.

  4. Commit Before Invalidate ↗

    Entitlements persists overrides via SaveChangesAsync, evicts FeatureCache, and bumps admin:principal:* version stamps to stop stale tokens immediately.

How do permissions transition across all five lifecycle states?

Diagram structure
  • Defined defined
  • Available available
  • Assignable assignable
  • Assigned assigned
  • Effective effective
  • PlatformOnly platform_only_blocked
  • Feature Off feature_disabled
  • Cache Evict cache_evicting
  • Denied 403 denied_403
  • defined → available · Entitled
  • defined → platform_only_blocked · PlatformOnly
  • defined → feature_disabled · Flag Off
  • available → assignable · Scoped
  • assignable → assigned · Granted
  • assigned → effective · Enforced
  • effective → feature_disabled · Override Off
  • feature_disabled → available · Re-Enabled
  • effective → cache_evicting · Mutated
  • cache_evicting → effective · Re-Synced
  • effective → denied_403 · Refusal 403

Every catalog permission travels from compile-time definition into active tenant pools, pickers, persisted roles, and runtime enforcement while isolating PlatformOnly and disabled features non-destructively.

  1. Defined (490 Perms) ↗

    Catalog providers declare explicit RequiredFeature, RequiredAnyFeatures (10), or IsGloballyAvailable (10) predicates.

  2. Available (389 SCRIPE) ↗

    TenantPermissionManager syncs satisfied !PlatformOnly permissions into TenantPermissions and T_SCRIPE_SA.

  3. PlatformOnly (69 Exit) ↗

    Host permissions exit before entering TenantPermissions, UI pickers, Break-Glass elevation, or tenant execution.

  4. Non-Destructive Disable ↗

    Turning a feature off revokes Effective access immediately while keeping custom RolePermissions rows intact for restore.

One canonical merge pipeline normalizes dotted resource names without splitting on dots and applies identical masking across JSON APIs, writes, and exported files.

Critical Oracle & Sovereign Isolation Boundaries

Never compare submitted restricted values against stored database values inside UpdateOpportunityCommandHandler, because differing HTTP status codes leak secret field values. Never grant PlatformOnly permissions to any tenant role, UserGroup, AdminDelegation, or MembershipMode context, and keep T_SCRIPE_SA locked out of platform-admin actions.
